page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-32-highlssd is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the z4d server family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. The instance is equipped with 252.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of approximately 7.88 GB per vCPU. This configuration does not include any graphics processing units and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Local storage is supported via NVMe SSD interfaces, though specific local storage capacity is not defined in the hardware profile.

With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of nearly 1:8, this server type is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial RAM capacity relative to compute cores. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance without resource contention from neighboring tenants. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density per core allows organizations to run large-scale in-memory databases and caching layers without paying for excess vCPUs, optimizing software licensing and compute resource costs.

The z4d-highmem-32-highlssd is engineered for workloads such as high-performance databases, in-memory data stores like Redis or Memcached, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-bound data processing pipelines. The combination of dedicated x86_64 cores, large memory capacity, and NVMe SSD compatibility makes it suitable for transaction-heavy database operations and real-time analytics.
